task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series winning?
How should adherence be measured, and how should it be conditioned on opponent strength and game state?
Is the 54-series unit sufficient for a test of this association at useful power?
Can the recommendation effect be separated from the inherent suppression value of the recommended options?

historical_evidence.finding: Possession-level test of whether engine-recommended PTs score more than other PTs within a series. Crude difference +0.140 PPP [0.084, 0.196]; DiD vs regular season +0.090 [0.041, 0.141]; strictest two-way FE gamma +0.0088, SE 0.0239, p=0.7139 on 504 cells from 74 team-series pairs. Record attributes the A and B effects to the engine picking high-PPP PTs. Recorded failure type: B_powered_null.

Within-series test of whether teams shifting toward the engine's prescribed mix win more and improve PPP. Win rate 50.0% vs 50.0% after shift. Only 8 rows had a SHOULD vector prescription (aligned 4/6 wins vs 1/2); 96 of 104 rows had none. Record notes 'Sample too small at this gate'. Recorded failure type: A_unanswerable.

Matchup-specific (non-CUT) BEST counters vs a feasibility-weighted league mix. Headline all-BEST gap +0.269 (p=0.0000, n=283) is recorded as CUT-driven. Non-CUT gap +0.010 (p=0.1709, n=136); L3 matchup non-CUT gap +0.001 (p=0.3277, n=47). Recorded failure type: B_powered_null. Record was truncated ('1 [cut; read_family for the full text]'); I did not read the full text.

Descriptive check of whether observed play-type mix in a game matches the recommended opener. Average absolute gap across leverage buckets 4.5pp to 24.0pp; 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank-1. Single 2025-26 playoff G1s, about 100 possessions per game, with no outcome comparison. Recorded failure type: E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Possession-level test that engine-recommended PTs outscore other PTs within series, beyond inherent PT value
failed_approaches.why: Adequately powered null (B_powered_null) after controls: strictest FE estimate near zero. Earlier positive effects were explained by selection of high-PPP PTs by the engine.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-series shift toward the prescribed mix as a test of winning and PPP improvement
failed_approaches.why: Unanswerable at the design gate (A_unanswerable): only 8 of 104 rows had a prescription vector, and the sample was too small.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matchup-specific BEST counters beating a constrained league mix, once CUT plays are excluded
failed_approaches.why: Adequately powered null on the non-CUT subset (B_powered_null). The headline effect was CUT-driven, so the matchup-specificity claim did not hold.

evidence_establishes: Earlier family records in this project tested recommendation-adherence and recommended-mix claims at the possession, team-series and single-game levels. None tested series winning as the outcome.

Where recommended-option effects appeared in earlier records, they were recorded as attributable to selection on high-value options (SF-[prior work]) or to a CUT-driven headline (SF-[prior work]), not to adherence.
Samples of this type (about 74 team-series pairs, 8 prescription-bearing rows, n=47-283 on subsets) gave underpowered or unanswerable tests in earlier records.
evidence_does_not_establish: Any association between adherence to a suppression-conditional mix and series winning. No retrieved record reports a series-level outcome test of adherence.
Whether 54 series is enough for a series-level binary-outcome test. No record reports a power calculation for series outcomes.
Whether the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data differ in recommendation quality or play-type mix over time.
The full content of SF-[prior work], which was truncated in retrieval. I did not call read_family.
own_inferences: Series winning is a single binary outcome per series. With 54 series, a modest adherence effect (for example, 5 to 10 percentage points on win probability) cannot be distinguished from zero at conventional power.
Adherence measured as the share of possessions on recommended PTs is confounded with team quality and opponent strength, since stronger teams may both follow better recommendations and win more.

The recommended mix is derived from suppression value, so adherence may be a proxy for choosing high-PPP options. Earlier records (SF-[prior work]) suggest this selection mechanism is what drove apparent effects.
uncertainties: Retrieval returned only four records, and none tested series outcomes directly. Whether other relevant family records exist in this setting is unknown.
SF-[prior work] was truncated. Its full content may contain details that change the assessment.
Exact per-series counts of adherence-measurable possessions in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data are not stated in the retrieved records.
Whether the playoff data window (2025-26 playoffs partial until 2026-06-21) is complete at the date of analysis is not established by [prior work].

historical_effect.explanation: Earlier records show that the same recommendation-based claims were either powered nulls, unanswerable at small n, or descriptive only. They also show that apparent effects were explained by selection and CUT-driven headlines. This moved the decision away from proceeding with a direct series-level test and toward do_not_proceed as posed. A redesigned, pre-specified test with explicit selection controls is the minimum viable route.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series gives a binary outcome with very low power for a modest adherence effect. Earlier records of similar scale (SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work]) were unanswerable or underpowered.
The recommendation selects high-PPP options, so adherence is correlated with option value. Earlier SF-[prior work] effects were explained by this selection.
Team quality and opponent strength plausibly affect both adherence and series outcome. No record reports adjustment for these.
Prescription vectors were present on only 8 of 104 rows in SF-[prior work], so most units lack the exposure needed to measure adherence.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests adherence to a suppression-conditional mix against series winning. Related earlier tests of recommended-mix value at possession, team-series and single-game levels returned powered nulls (SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work]), an unanswerable design (SF-[prior work]) or a descriptive result (SF-[prior work]). Together they partly answer the question in the negative for the recommendation's incremental value, but they do not test series outcomes directly.

risks.text: 54 series units, with a binary outcome, cannot detect a plausible adherence effect at useful power.
Engine picks high-value options, so adherence may proxy for option quality rather than the recommendation's counter value.
Team strength and opponent quality can drive both adherence and winning.
Adherence as a share of recommended PTs depends on the play-type tagger, which records earlier note as having a floor on some play types (SF-[prior work]).
Prescription vectors are missing for most rows, so adherence is not measurable for most units.
If adherence is computed over the full series, later games may reflect the series result and inflate the association.
Several definitions of adherence, conditioning sets and subsets (CUT vs non-CUT, leverage buckets) raise the false-positive risk.
Pooling 2022-23 through 2025-26 and mixing regular season and playoffs may change the recommendation's effect over time.
Series winners are 50% by construction over a bracket, so the effect must be measured against a matched or seed-adjusted baseline.

design.estimand: Not proceeding as posed. Minimum viable estimand: within-team-game association between adherence to the recommended PT mix and possession-level points per possession, conditional on the PT's inherent PPP, regular-season baseline and opponent strength. Series winning is reported only as descriptive context.
design.unit: Team-game (or team-possession) within series, not series-level alone.
design.sample: 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs, restricted to games with a recorded prescription vector. Sample size must be counted before analysis; earlier records indicate this may be small.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum detectable effect and compute power on the counted units before any run. If the counted series are below the threshold, the test is reported as untestable rather than run.
design.controls: Inherent PT PPP (regular-season baseline), opponent defensive strength, seed or team quality, game state, team fixed effects. Adherence computed on games strictly before the outcome game to avoid lookahead.
design.falsification: Null association between adherence and PPP after PT-value controls, and a placebo test using random recommended mixes of matched PT value.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered primary adherence definition and outcome. Other definitions, CUT and non-CUT splits, and leverage buckets are secondary and corrected for multiple comparisons.
design.decision_rule: Support requires a positive adherence coefficient beyond PT-value controls with the placebo null rejected at the pre-set threshold. Otherwise report as rejected (if powered) or untestable (if underpowered). Series-level winning is reported descriptively only.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files: 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs, as available on 2026-06-16. 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21, so partial playoff data before that date must be excluded or flagged.
